quarterly_data.signal: Q4 2025 results: revenue of $1.03 billion, up 5% sequentially and 10% year-over-year, with revenue, gross margin and earnings per diluted share all above the midpoint of guidance and demand up across all 3 end markets. Semiconductor revenue was $435 million (up 5% sequentially and 9% year-over-year), above the high end of guidance on strengthening DRAM and logic/foundry demand; Electronics & Packaging revenue was $303 million (up 5% quarter-over-quarter and 19% year-over-year) on higher flexible PCB drilling and chemistry equipment sales; Specialty Industrial revenue was $295 million (up 4% sequentially and 5% year-over-year) on research and defense, with automotive soft. Gross margin was 46.4%, down year-over-year on higher tariffs, zero-margin palladium pass-through and a higher chemistry-equipment mix; operating margin 21%; adjusted EBITDA $249 million (24.1% margin); net earnings $168 million or $2.47 per diluted share.
quarterly_data.figure: Q4 revenue $1.03 billion, up 5% sequentially and 10% year-over-year; semiconductor $435 million, up 5% sequentially and 9% year-over-year; Electronics & Packaging $303 million, an increase of 5% quarter-over-quarter and 19% year-over-year; Specialty Industrial $295 million; gross margin 46.4%; $2.47 per diluted share

quarterly_data.signal: Semiconductor demand color: Q4 semiconductor strength came primarily from subsystems serving etch and deposition applications in the DRAM and logic foundry markets, led by plasma and reactive gases, with healthy momentum in dissolved gases for advanced logic and in back-end applications related to high bandwidth memory ('Order activity in both areas remains robust'); NAND-related activity was stable sequentially, and Q1 2026 semiconductor revenue is expected to be up sequentially. CEO John Lee said customers are putting heavy investment into DRAM for AI, which is causing a memory availability crunch, and 'NAND has become potentially a bottleneck as well'; one large (unnamed) chip company announced a brand-new greenfield NAND factory, which extends the ramps. MKS's position in RF power for NAND vertical channel etching 'allows us to enjoy upgrades almost as much as greenfield', and NAND is expected to be 'icing on the cake' through the year and the next couple of years. MKS says its semiconductor business outperformed estimated WFE growth in 2025 and that it is positioned in leading-edge foundry and high-bandwidth memory investment through its vacuum and Photonics offerings.

WFE ramp and capacity: CEO John Lee said a couple of MKS's etch customers (transcribed as 'edge customers') are talking about 20% year-over-year WFE growth and a couple of litho/metrology customers (transcribed as 'listometrology') about the mid-teens, with the cycle expected to last longer than one year; 'the ramp has started', customer conversations about getting ready began in Q4 and accelerated in Q1, but MKS was still shipping to demand in the early stages of the ramp. MKS outperforms in upturns because it must ship ahead of its customers and customers build inventory; to support a 20% WFE increase MKS has to get to a '5 handle' in quarterly semiconductor revenue 'probably', with timing not predictable, and 'if we could ship more, our customers will probably take it.' Capacity: MKS got ready for $125 billion run-rate WFE 3 years ago and always keeps 30% surge capacity on top, so plant capacity is not the constraint - the challenge is getting the supply chain to ramp. The new Malaysia supercenter factory ramps in the second half of 2026 (online midyear); it was built as a footprint/resiliency move and for future WFE capacity needs and has not been sized yet.
quarterly_data.figure: a couple of etch ('edge' as transcribed) customers citing 20% year-over-year WFE growth; semiconductor revenue needs a 5 handle; capacity for $125 billion WFE run rate plus 30% surge capacity

quarterly_data.signal: Q1 2026 guidance: revenue of $1.04 billion, plus or minus $40 million; Electronics & Packaging $305 million, plus or minus $15 million (up slightly sequentially despite the Lunar New Year and up in the low 20% range year-over-year, on higher flexible PCB drilling revenue and continued strong chemistry equipment); Specialty Industrial $285 million, plus or minus $10 million (down low to mid-single digits sequentially, up mid-single digits year-over-year); semiconductor revenue expected up sequentially (the transcript prints the semiconductor guide as '$150 million, plus or minus $15 million', which does not reconcile with the $1.04 billion total; the CEO later says 'we're guiding 450'). Operating expenses $270 million plus or minus $5 million, adjusted EBITDA $251 million plus or minus $24 million, EPS $2 plus or minus $0.28, tax rate approximately 21% (18% to 20% for the year). The gross-margin guide is garbled in the transcript ('4% to 6% plus or minus 100 basis points'); the CFO attributed the lower Q1 margin to seasonally lower chemistry mix from the Lunar New Year, with mix expected to improve in Q2 and further in Q3. Capital expenditures are expected to average 4% to 5% of revenue through 2026, and operating expenses to grow slower than revenue.
quarterly_data.figure: Q1 revenue $1.04 billion, plus or minus $40 million; Electronics & Packaging $305 million, plus or minus $15 million; Specialty Industrial $285 million, plus or minus $10 million; EPS $2 plus or minus $0.28; capex 4% to 5% of revenue through 2026

quarterly_data.signal: Electronics & Packaging and AI boards: excluding FX and palladium pass-through, chemistry sales increased 16% in Q4 and 11% for full-year 2025, while E&P grew 20% - the rest of that growth being capacity additions of chemistry equipment and flex drilling equipment. Orders for chemistry and chemistry equipment for advanced PCBs related to AI kept their momentum; 'AI is driving increasing packaging complexity', and AI is driving demand for more complex PCBs with rapidly increasing layer counts despite multiyear softness in smartphones and PCs. CEO John Lee framed the content opportunity by layer count: smartphone PCBs are around 10 to 12 layers and go up a couple of layers every cycle, AI also needs multilayer boards of 30 to 40 layers plus package-substrate layers, and for AI 'we're talking about doubling the number of layers'; AI's share of chemistry revenue rose sequentially quarter after quarter in 2025 and is expected to keep taking a larger share, with AI chemistry more than making up for any slight decrease in PCs and smartphones because AI supply-chain customers are running at capacity and continue to add tools. Flex drilling is in a 'normalized cycle' rather than a super cycle, with foldable phones driving more flex demand.
quarterly_data.figure: chemistry sales up 16% in Q4 and 11% for 2025 excluding FX and palladium; smartphone PCBs 10 to 12 layers vs AI multilayer boards 30 to 40 layers

quarterly_data.signal: Chemistry equipment as the leading indicator: MKS is in its 'fifth quarter of strong bookings and revenue' for chemistry equipment, its factories were full through the first half of 2026, and bookings remained strong versus 90 days earlier, which could mean 'potentially 2 good years of record level chemistry equipment shipments' (management will no longer guide equipment bookings). The attach model is unchanged: $20 million to $40 million of chemistry sales per year per $100 million of equipment sales when the tool runs at full utilization, with little difference by board type, and equipment takes 18 to 24 months to turn into chemistry revenue - so 2025 chemistry growth came from equipment shipped in 2021 and 2022, and today's shipments underpin chemistry in 2026, 2027 and beyond. MKS added some E&P equipment capacity without needing a new factory, is meeting customer timing even at elevated levels and is 'not constraining our customers'.
quarterly_data.figure: $20 million to $40 million of chemistry per $100 million of equipment sales at full utilization; 18 to 24 months from equipment shipment to chemistry revenue

quarterly_data.signal: Panel-level advanced packaging: many customers are working on moving redistribution layers from wafer-shaped to rectangular panel formats, and 'when they go to panel, that's MKS' - MKS participates in wafer-type packaging but its strength has always been panels, so the shift is a tailwind. It is still relatively small for MKS because it is only 1 or 2 layers of redistribution, while HDI and multilayer boards and package substrates are adding layers much faster (as transcribed: 'HDI and MOB are growing at 10 layers a year or more each').
quarterly_data.figure: panel RDL is 1 or 2 layers; HDI and multilayer board layer counts growing at 10 layers a year or more

quarterly_data.signal: Full-year 2025 and balance sheet: revenue $3.9 billion, up 10% year-over-year, with 20% EPS growth and over 20% free cash flow growth; gross margin 46.7%, down 90 basis points on tariffs and mix including record chemistry equipment sales (tariffs still weigh on gross margin by about 50 basis points); operating margin 20.7%; operating cash flow $645 million and free cash flow $497 million, up 21%. Specialty Industrial revenue was $1.1 billion, down 4% on industrial softness including automotive. Liquidity was approximately $1.4 billion, net debt $3.6 billion and net leverage 3.7x on full-year adjusted EBITDA of $966 million; MKS made $400 million of term-loan prepayments in 2025 and another $100 million in February 2026 (over $1 billion paid down since February 2024), issued EUR 1 billion of senior unsecured notes, repriced its term loan and increased the revolver to $1 billion - together reducing annual interest expense by approximately $27 million on a run-rate basis - and the Board authorized a 14% dividend increase.
quarterly_data.figure: 2025 revenue $3.9 billion, up 10%; gross margin 46.7%; free cash flow $497 million; net leverage 3.7x on adjusted EBITDA of $966 million
